item.text: I’m reviewing the extracted layout before changing it. The next refactor needs to reduce real complexity now that the API surface is split across two classes.

I found a worthwhile cleanup in the boundary between the two classes: `BalancedParentheses` still needs two separate profile queries to classify one character. I’m moving bracket classification fully into `BracketProfile` so the validator consumes one token model instead of probing multiple collections.
I’m reshaping `BracketProfile` now so it produces stable classification tokens up front. That lets the validator stop knowing about the profile’s internal maps and sets.
The token model is in place. I’m reading the updated sources once before compiling, mainly to catch any cleanup issues from the profile rewrite rather than waiting for the compiler to do all of it.
There’s one cleanup from the rewrite: `BracketProfile` has a small formatting issue and the imports can be normalized. I’m fixing that before verification so the refactor lands in a clean state.
I’m compiling and running the suite now. I’ll also do the usual CLI sanity check after the profile classification change.

item.text:
Refactored the boundary between [BalancedParentheses.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParentheses.java:1) and [BracketProfile.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BracketProfile.java:1) so bracket classification now lives entirely in `BracketProfile`. `BalancedParentheses` no longer does multiple profile lookups per character; it consumes a single `BracketToken` model and only handles stack validation.

That makes the responsibilities cleaner: `BracketProfile` owns how characters are interpreted, and `BalancedParentheses` only owns balance checking. The existing tests in [BalancedParenthesesTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/042_balanced_parentheses/BalancedParenthesesTest.java:1) still cover standard behavior, custom profiles, invalid profiles, `CharSequence` inputs, and null handling.

Verified with:
```sh
mkdir -p build/test-classes && javac -cp lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar -d build/test-classes BracketProfile.java BalancedParentheses.java BalancedParenthesesTest.java && java -jar lib/junit-platform-console-standalone-1.10.2.jar execute --class-path build/test-classes --scan-class-path
```
All 12 tests passed. I also sanity-checked `main` with `java -cp build/test-classes BalancedParentheses "{[()]}"`, which returned `true`.
